request.system: You design a structured interview blueprint. Given a job profile and a target number of main questions, produce exactly that many question slots that together give broad, non-overlapping coverage of the role's most important skills and focus areas. Order them to flow naturally — foundational topics before advanced ones. Calibrate each difficulty to the stated seniority. Each slot names the specific skill to test, the intent (what to assess), a difficulty, and the key points a strong answer should cover — the concepts, tradeoffs, and edge cases later used to grade the candidate's answer.

messages.content:
Job context:
- Company: Streamside Media
- Target role: Senior Machine Learning Engineer
- Seniority: senior
- Key skills to assess: Python, Learning-to-rank, Recommender systems, A/B testing, Model serving, Low-latency inference, Feature pipelines, Model training, Offline evaluation, Online evaluation, Model monitoring, Kubernetes
- Focus areas: Production machine learning, Ranking models, End-to-end model ownership, Personalization at scale, System design for ML, Model deployment, Performance evaluation

Design exactly 3 interview question slots for this role.

skill.description: The specific skill or topic this question tests, e.g. 'Kubernetes networking'.
skill.title: Skill

intent.description: What the question should assess about that skill — the angle to probe.
intent.title: Intent

difficulty.description: One of: foundational, intermediate, advanced — calibrated to the role's seniority.
difficulty.title: Difficulty

key_points.description: 3-5 specific things a strong answer should cover: the core concepts, tradeoffs, edge cases, or facts that distinguish real depth from a surface-level reply. Each a short phrase. Used later to grade answers, so be concrete and answer-focused, not a restatement of the question.
key_points.title: Key Points

slots.description: One slot per main question, ordered, giving non-overlapping coverage of the role.
slots.title: Slots

slots.intent: Assess ability to design and implement ranking models for personalization at scale, including understanding of loss functions, feature engineering, and real-world tradeoffs between relevance and diversity
key_points: Choice of ranking loss (pointwise, pairwise, listwise) and justification for production context
Feature engineering for ranking: static vs. dynamic features, feature importance in candidate generation vs. reranking
Balancing relevance, diversity, and business metrics (engagement, CTR, revenue); cold-start and exploration-exploitation tradeoffs
Online vs. offline evaluation gaps and designing metrics to catch them

slots.intent: Evaluate design thinking for deploying ranking or recommendation models in production with strict latency budgets, including caching, batching, and system architecture choices
key_points: Candidate generation (retrieval) vs. reranking pipeline; latency breakdown and bottleneck identification
Caching strategies (embedding caches, pre-computed candidates) and staleness tradeoffs
Batch inference, request coalescing, and serving framework choices (KServe, TensorFlow Serving, custom); Kubernetes deployment patterns
Monitoring latency, throughput, and model staleness; graceful degradation under load

slots.skill: End-to-end model lifecycle and evaluation strategy
slots.intent: Assess comprehensive ownership of a model from training through monitoring, including offline evaluation design, A/B testing rigor, and production incident response
key_points: Designing offline evaluation to correlate with online metrics; pitfalls of train/test leakage and temporal bias
A/B test design: sample size, statistical power, guardrail metrics, and interaction effects
Feature pipeline reliability, data freshness, and retraining triggers; monitoring model decay and performance degradation
Canary deployments, rollback criteria, and shadow mode testing to reduce production risk
